types.embedding_query_text: Athlete: A person who plays a sport professionally or at an elite level Also called sportsman, player, footballer, professional athlete, national team member. Examples: Neymar, Thierry Henry, Zlatan Ibrahimović, Brazilian icon.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Athletes are individuals, and 'Person' directly matches the definition and examples of specific athletes.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: Country Examples: Brazil, Norway, Brazilian men's national team.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The examples 'Brazil' and 'Norway' are sovereign states, aligning perfectly with the schema.org Country class.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: SportsTournament: A multi-match competition in a sport Also called world cup, olympic tournament, international competition, cup, championship. Examples: 2026 World Cup, World Cup Today, World Cup tournaments.

chosen_type.label: SportsEvent
chosen_type.justification: A sports tournament is a specific type of athletic competition, fitting the schema.org SportsEvent definition which includes 'tennis tournament' as an example.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The examples include calendar dates (e.g., '2026-07-05') and years ('2010'), aligning with the schema.org Date class for calendar dates without time components.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: ShippingDeliveryTime
candidates.comment: A structured value providing details about the expected delivery times for product shipping. Also called delivery timeframe, estimated delivery, shipping lead time, transit time. Examples: 'ships in 1-2 business days', 'delivery by Friday', 'estimated 3-5 day transit'.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

chosen_type.label: SportsStatistic
chosen_type.definition: A numerical measure representing a player's performance in sports, such as goals or appearances.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents sports statistics like '80 goals' or '129 appearances'; 'SportsStatistic' captures this distinct usage.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: MedicalStudyStatus
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".

chosen_type.label: StadiumOrArena
chosen_type.justification: The example 'Miami Stadium' is a large civic structure for sports events, matching the schema.org StadiumOrArena definition.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: MusicVenue
candidates.comment: A MusicVenue is a civic structure or place specifically designed for musical performances. Also called concert hall, live music venue, performance space. Examples: Carnegie Hall, a local bar with live bands, an outdoor amphitheater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The example '34 years' represents a time span, aligning with the schema.org Duration class for periods of time.

candidates.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
candidates.comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. Also called adult content classification, age restriction type, mature content indicator. Examples: `AdultSexualContent`, `ViolentContent`, `GamblingContent`.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: DatedMoneySpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary amount that is valid or applicable over a specified time period, though its use is superseded by MonetaryAmount. Also called Time-bound monetary value, period-specific money, dated financial amount. Examples: An employee's salary from 2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, a subscription fee valid for a quarter, a bonus paid for a specific fiscal year.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A recognition given for excellence in a field Also called prize, honor, trophy, title, accolade. Examples: Ballon d'Or.

chosen_type.label: Award
chosen_type.definition: A recognition given for excellence in a field, such as the Ballon d'Or.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents awards like the Ballon d'Or; 'Award' captures this distinct concept as a recognition.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: Grant
candidates.comment: A Grant is an intangible, typically financial or quantifiable, allocation of resources from a funder to an organization or person, often supporting specific collective goals or projects. Also called funding award, financial aid, sponsorship, endowment. Examples: research grant, arts grant, student scholarship, disaster relief fund.

chosen_type.label: SportsMedal
chosen_type.definition: A medal awarded for achievement in a sports competition, such as a silver medal in the World Cup.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class represents sports medals; 'SportsMedal' captures this distinct award type with specific examples.

candidates.label: RsvpResponseType
candidates.comment: An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type. Examples: RsvpResponseType.Yes, RsvpResponseType.No, RsvpResponseType.MayBe.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration is an Enumeration of modes for organizing an event, indicating whether it is online or offline. Also called attendance type, event format, participation mode. Examples: OnlineEventAttendanceMode, OfflineEventAttendanceMode, MixedEventAttendanceMode.

candidates.label: EmployerAggregateRating
candidates.comment: An EmployerAggregateRating is an AggregateRating representing a collective assessment of an Organization's performance as an employer. Also called company rating, employer review score, workplace satisfaction rating. Examples: Glassdoor's overall rating for a company, an average employee satisfaction score, a composite rating from multiple employee surveys.

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.
